validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: independently confirmed by two origins that both name the project. (1) The Federal Register's publication of FERC's notice of NGPL's Nov. 15, 2019 blanket-certificate prior-notice filing (Docket CP20-14-000): 'Natural requests authorization to construct, own, operate, modify, and maintain an approximately 1.4 mile, 12-inch diameter pipeline lateral and appurtenant facilities...in Cook County, Illinois and Lake County, Indiana (134th Street Lateral Project)...a new delivery interconnection between Natural and Northern Indiana Public Service Company (NIPSCO)...estimated cost...approximately $16.2 million.' (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' sheet, row for 'Gas: 134th Street Lateral Project' — operator 'Nat Gas P L Co of America', Status Completed, Completed Date 2021-08-20, Year In Service 2021, State(s) IL/IN, Cost (millions) 16.2, Miles 1.4, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 70, Pipeline Diameter (Inches) 20, Docket Number CP20-14, Crosses State Border Yes, Project Notes 'New lateral to replace existing pipeline; deliveries to NIPSCO in IN.' These two origins independently corroborate length, cost, docket number, project name, and general geography — this is a real, completed, in-service FERC-jurisdictional lateral, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an interstate natural-gas transmission lateral (Fuel=Gas) — both sources describe a NGA section 7 / blanket-certificate natural-gas facility delivering to an LDC (NIPSCO), not a gathering or processing line. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of the two sibling Gulf Coast Southbound rows in this roster — P2039 (Phase I, FERC Docket CP16-488, EIA: $149M, 460 MMcf/d added capacity, completed 2018-10-04, a mainline REVERSAL/compression project Illinois-to-Texas) and P2541 (Phase II, FERC Docket CP19-99, EIA: $176M, 300 MMcf/d added capacity, completed 2021-03-01, also a mainline reversal/compression project) are both large system-wide southbound-capacity expansions on NGPL's mainline. P2495 is docket CP20-14, a physically distinct, separately-filed, much smaller LOCAL delivery lateral (1.4 mi, $16.2M) built to interconnect with NIPSCO — a different facility under a different docket, not a relabeling of either Phase I or Phase II. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 'Natural Gas Pipeline Co of America LLC (NGPL)' at 100% is correct and independently confirmed by both sources (the FERC filing's applicant of record and the EIA operator field). CAVEATS carried into separate validity records below: (1) a material Diameter conflict between the two sources (12in per the literal 2019 FERC application text vs 20in per the EIA compiled record, which is what the sheet currently carries); (2) EndState/Province is misspelled 'Inidiana' and EndPrefecture/District is blank — both sources agree the project genuinely crosses into Lake County, Indiana (to reach the NIPSCO interconnect), so the fix is the spelling and the missing county, NOT a change to Illinois as this batch's brief speculated for this row.

validity.researcher_notes: The two sources that independently confirm this project's existence DISAGREE on diameter. The Federal Register's verbatim quotation of NGPL's Nov. 2019 application states 'an approximately 1.4 mile, 12-inch diameter pipeline lateral' — a specific, literal figure from the actual regulatory filing. The EIA compiled workbook instead lists 'Pipeline Diameter (Inches): 20' for the same named project and docket — and 20 is what the sheet currently carries, so the sheet's Diameter appears to trace to the EIA compilation rather than to the underlying FERC filing. It is possible the design was amended upward between the 2019 application and 2021 completion, or that EIA's compiled figure is simply in error (EIA's project-tracking workbook is a compiled secondary source, not the filing itself) — either is plausible and this could not be adjudicated further without the actual FERC docket record. Flagging as a material disagreement rather than silently keeping 20in.
